title.narrative: Capacity Building for Evidence Based Policy Making in Education and Health Sectors in the OECS

description.narrative: "The objective of the IDF grant is to develop capacity for evidence-based policy making in the education sector and health sector in the OECS countries (St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Lucia, Grenada, and St. Vincent and the Grenadines). The OECS region suffers severely from lack of updated, reliable data for decision making in the social sectors, particularly in education and health. Management information systems are of questionable quality and there are no mechanisms to crosscheck what data exists. While there have been efforts to improve availability of data, there are problems with the quality of information and there is very limited use of data to inform policy decisions. The lack of reliable and timely information hampers efforts to improve outcomes in education and health. The OECS Secretariat's Social and Sustainable Development Division (SSDD), together with sectoral policy-makers in member countries, is now engaged in strengthening the use of evidence in policy making. A recent paper presented by the OECS Secretariat and endorsed by the OECS Head of Government ""Towards a New OECS Education Development Agenda"" emphasizes evidence-based policy making in education, and similar efforts are underway in health. However, the capacity to achieve this is lacking, and the stakeholders-both within the OECS and at the country level-have requested technical support. The proposed grant will help to improve the availability and use of statistical data and statistical skills on a sustainable basis at both country level and in the OECS Secretariat. The proposed activities will build OECS countries' capacity in data collection and analysis for policy making in education and health. Teams from the ministries of education and health, as well as corresponding units at the OECS Secretariat, will be taken through a full cycle of evidence-based policy making at the end of which they will have developed capacity to collect, analyze and interpret data for use in improvement of their programs. The OECS is mandated to coordinate education and health activities, including development of regional strategies in these two sectors, and will therefore coordinate this work. IDF funds will be used to provide technical assistance for training and guidance at different stages of this process. The process will involve identifying policy learning needs, hands-on training, and use of the results to feed back into the policy making process. four OECS countries (St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Lucia, Grenada, and St. Vincent and the Grenadines)."
